title: customer-network-event-curation-playbook
body:
Purpose: Draft playbook to define a single operational pattern for curating, retaining, and exporting network-related audit events in Private deployments (customer-managed VPCs / on-prem). This focuses on three product needs: 1) tamper-evident audit traces for customer and ops investigations, 2) an approval-gate state model that integrates with customer change requests, and 3) pragmatic retention/cost controls that respect customer bandwidth and legal constraints.

Scope: Applies to Private control-plane interactions, operator-initiated changes routed to customer-managed networking (peers, firewall rules, routing changes, handshakes), and the on-prem edge collector that surfaces telemetry back to Redwood for observability & forensic exports. Not in scope: hosted public API request logs, unrelated application payloads, or non-networking telemetry.

Overview of approach:
- Event curation: collect low-level change events (API call, operator id, timestamp, diff), related evidence (config snapshots, certificate chain, packet-sampled proof when available), and a minimal context blob linking to a change request.
- Curation tiers (customer-selectable):
  - Tier 1 (Operational): 90-day retention, 1:100 sampling for pre-change telemetry, aggregated diffs, no raw packet captures.
  - Tier 2 (Forensic): 365-day retention, 1:10 sampling, full config snapshots, signed diffs.
  - Tier 3 (Legal-Hold): indefinite retention, full evidence capsule, optional packet capture, exportable immutable bundle.

Data model and evidence capsule:
- Each curated event is stored as a JSONL record: event_meta, actor, change_delta, snapshot_ref, signature, provenance_chain_id.
- Evidence capsule: a downloadable .tgz containing JSONL, gzipped configs, and a signed manifest. Manifest contains a sequence number, SHA256 digests, KMS key id (customer or Redwood), and optional Merkle root for batch verification.

Tamper evidence and cryptography:
- Default: sequence numbers + SHA256 per-event + Redwood KMS signing.
- Customer-managed option: customer KMS/HSM binding; Redwood only stores signature metadata (not private keys).
- Optional Merkle-chain mode for customers needing compact cross-event proofs (useful for legal/audit export).

Approval gates & state machine (high level):
- States: DRAFT -> PRE_APPROVAL -> SCHEDULED -> APPLYING -> MONITORING -> ROLLBACK_PENDING -> COMPLETED -> AUDIT_STORED
- Transitions require actor identity + justification comment + approval token. Approval tokens may be single-signer, multi-signer (n-of-m), or automated policy-based approvals (policy-evaluated).
- For customer-managed nets, the agent will include a handshake step: customer operator must ACK the schedule before APPLYING (configurable bypass for emergency mode).

Operator and Customer UX flows:
- Operator console: compact timeline per-change showing curated artifacts, sampling level, approval status, and export button (generate evidence capsule).
- Customer admin: consent panel to choose curation tier, bind KMS, set retention windows and emergency bypass rules, and audit-export role mapping.

Bandwidth, storage and cost guidance (approx):
- Example assumptions: 10k changes/month, typical curated record 2–6 KB, full snapshot 0.5–5 MB per change.
- Tier 1 cost estimate: ~50 GB/mo per 10k changes. Tier 2: ~2.5 TB/mo. Tier 3: grows with legal-hold volume (recommend lifecycle policies).
- Provide default auto-archive policy to S3-IA or Glacier for Tier 3 after 1 year unless legal hold locked.

Search, replay and verification tooling:
- Lightweight replayer: apply diffs against a sandboxed config model to reproduce operator-visible state changes (local mode for privacy).
- Verify tool: consumes evidence capsules, validates signatures and manifest checksums, optionally runs Merkle verification.

Compliance mapping and edge cases:
- Map curation tiers to SOC2/ISO/PCI expectations; Tier2+ recommended for SOC2 evidence retention for network changes.
- GDPR: Data minimization options (truncate user identifiers), region-specific retention defaults, and legal hold exempt flags.

Operational concerns and risk mitigations:
- Collector outages: buffer events locally with ring buffer; backpressure policy and alerting to both Redwood SRE and customer admin.
- Spikes: adaptive sampling to avoid saturating customer uplink; provide explicit quotas in private contract.
- Proof-of-possession: periodic signed heartbeat from edge agent to detect tampering or rollback attempts.

Open questions & unresolved decisions:
- Legal hold storage billing model (customer-borne vs. Redwood-hosted premium).
- Whether to require Merkle chains for all Tier 3 exports or make optional.
- UI for multi-signer approvals: built-in modal vs. webhooks to customer IDP systems.

Immediate next steps and tickets:
- Spike: implement evidence capsule prototype and CLI verifier (GH PR linked above). Owner: Owen Park. (JIRA: PRIV-9021)
- Spec: formalize sequence number scheme and KMS binding UX. Owner: Marin Patel. (JIRA: PRIV-9033)
- UX: approval flow mockups and emergency bypass controls. Owner: Lina Gomez. (Figma link in Confluence page)

Notes to reviewers: This is a pragmatic, ops-ready draft intentionally focusing on exportability and minimal trust assumptions for customers. Feedback requested on retention tiers, signature model (customer KMS vs Redwood), and cost-estimate assumptions. Also please flag any regulatory needs we missed for APAC on-prem customers.

References and cross-links:
- Confluence: NET-EVIDENCE-OVERVIEW (linked above)
- Existing PRs: private-edge-agent/pull/119 (evidence capsule prototype)
- Slack thread: #priv-deploy-networking (search: "evidence capsule")

summary: Playbook draft outlining event curation tiers, tamper-evidence options, approval-state model, UX flows, cost guidance, and next steps for Private customer-managed networking audit traces.
